newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crudes revive late with NYMEX expiry.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crudes revive late with NYMEX expiry.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crudes rose late, tracking a revival in West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude ahead of NYMEX expiry on Friday.
But Alaska North Slope differentials lay dormant, with traders leaving early for the weekend while refiners appeared content with October supplies.
Spot WTI rose 15 cents from Thursday to $21.15/21.45 a barrel, as prices followed last-minute strength from the expiring NYMEX October contract.
Another light grade, Line 63, remained unchanged at $3.20 to $3.00 under October WTI, with postings at plus $1.00.
A major producer lowered its ANS offer under October WTI. Rumors were afoot that an ANS deal got done at $2.25 a barrel under WTI.
Prices for California Kern River crude remained $16.15/16.35 a barrel. And prices for lightly traded Wilmington crude oil held at $17.60/17.70.
